newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Istat warns of pensions timebomb.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Istat warns of pensions timebomb.

text.p: Recent revisions of the Italian state pension system have done little to curb long-term pension costs meaning structural reform is vital, the president of Italian statistics office Istat said on Tuesday.
Alberto Zuiliani told a parliamentary commission that pension reform in 1992 and 1995 had introduced only temporary curbs on early retirement.
"Part of the savings involved transitory suspensions (of benefits)...which could re-accelerate spending dynamics in the coming years," he said.
He said 2030 would be the crunch year, when baby boomers from the 1960s were retiring, putting an enormous burden on younger generations who would have to foot the pensions bill.
"Prospects will not be significantly improved, even if the birth rate picks up or there is greater immigration into Italy," Zuiliani said.
The centre-left government is due to start negotiations with unions and business leaders later this month on an overhaul of the welfare state, including pensions.

Zuiliani said the major worry remained the number of people who were being allowed to take early retirement. "This represents a sizeable burden on state accounts," he said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
